workPackageTitle: Command admission, sequence/idempotency, paused transaction shell
notes: Entries are added before implementation and are never renumbered (docs/technical/91 § Verification registry). This file is the first commit of the W1-SIM stream: no SIM production type or test class named by a selector below exists yet.
The structural validator for this file is owned by TASK-FND-009-002. Until it lands, the shape here matches tests/verification/FND-002.json and tests/verification/FND-003.json exactly.

Status is current status: every entry is 'registered' because no implementing task has landed. A later commit flips an entry to 'implemented' only when its selector actually runs and passes, as tests/verification/FND-002.json and tests/verification/FND-003.json do.

Every nunit selector is a fully qualified 'Namespace.Class.Method' so one entry names exactly one test method. Test namespaces mirror production namespaces per doc 114 § Naming and file-placement defaults; the full type and method layout the implementation must produce is fixed in the W1-SIM design contract handed to the implementation tasks.

doc 110 registers the SIM work packages but not their task IDs. SIM-004 splits into TASK-SIM-004-001, the active command path (command envelope of CTR-RUN-002, movement intent normalization, admission gate of CMP-SIM-002, typed rejection), and TASK-SIM-004-002, the paused transaction shell (request and result of CTR-RUN-003, expected state version, idempotency key). doc 110 lists both in one package because they share the admission gate, but they are separately landable.

The paused transaction entries assert the shell only: expected-state-version checking, atomicity between ticks, typed rejection, and idempotent replay. The domain validations doc 20 § Paused transactions lists - ownership, availability, slot capacity, duplication, cost, prerequisites, branch exclusivity, integer overflow - belong to the packages that own fabrication, relics, and PowerUps, and will register their own entries.

entries.summary: A command is applied at most once: resubmitting an envelope with the same run identity, target tick, and sequence is rejected as a duplicate and mutates nothing, including when the resubmission arrives in a later tick.
A stale, duplicate, or invalid envelope returns a typed rejection reason and leaves the admitted command set and the committed state byte-identical, so a rejection is never a partial mutation.

The command sequence is monotonic per run: a sequence at or below the highest already-admitted sequence is rejected, a gap is admitted without being backfilled, and no admitted envelope is ever reordered relative to another.
Run-session identity fences admission: an envelope carrying another run's identity is rejected on identity alone, without its payload being normalized or inspected.

Movement intent is normalized to a planar vector with magnitude in [0,1]: an over-unit analog magnitude clamps, each of the eight digital directions - including the four diagonals - normalizes to exactly unit length within a named tolerance, and zero input is an explicit stop rather than a tiny direction.

Commands are admitted and normalized in the first phase of the tick and are immutable thereafter: a command admitted for tick N is visible to tick N, is not visible to tick N-1, and no later phase can alter or append to that tick's admitted set.

A paused transaction is all-or-nothing between ticks: an accepted request publishes exactly one new state version with its domain events, a rejected one leaves the state version and every field unchanged, and no tick executes while the transaction is in flight.

A stale expected state version changes nothing and returns a typed rejection: the immutable view captured when the pause opened is refused once the authoritative version has moved on, and the caller learns why.

An idempotency key makes a replayed transaction observe the already-applied result rather than applying twice: the second submission returns the first result, the state version advances once, and the domain events are emitted once.
An accepted paused transaction publishes a replacement snapshot before resumption, so no tick ever runs against a state the presentation has not been given.

Over randomized envelope streams containing out-of-order, duplicated, stale, and foreign-run entries, the admitted sequence equals a deliberately simple reference model's and no rejected envelope ever mutated state, with the seed logged before the body runs.

A negative control proves the command gates can fail: a stub gate that keeps no deduplication history makes VER-SIM-004-001 fail, and a stub transaction that mutates before validating makes VER-SIM-004-007 and VER-SIM-004-008 fail.
